standard_prerequisites.name: The reduced induced closed subscheme structure on the closure of the image, and the factorization of a morphism into a reduced scheme through that closure, cited from the schemes chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the intermediate closed subscheme and the factorization through it.

standard_prerequisites.name: The description of an immersion as a morphism which factors through a closed immersion into an open subscheme of the target
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the open subscheme over which the factorization is by a closed immersion.

standard_prerequisites.name: Uniqueness of the reduced closed subscheme structure on a closed subset, cited from the schemes chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the image with the trace of the closure on the open subscheme.

core_obligations: Take the closure of the image with the reduced induced closed subscheme structure and factor the morphism through it using that the source is reduced (proof lines 288-292).
Use the definition of an immersion to find an open subscheme of the target through which the morphism factors by a closed immersion (proof lines 293-296).

Compare reduced closed subschemes: the trace of the closure on that open subscheme and the image are both reduced closed subschemes with the same underlying closed set, so by uniqueness they agree, which shows that the second factor of the factorization is an isomorphism onto its image, i.e. an open immersion (proof lines 297-303).
proof_roadmap: Factor through the reduced closure of the image and then use the local description of an immersion to identify the factorization as an open immersion followed by a closed immersion (proof lines 288-303).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that an immersion with reduced source factors as an open immersion followed by the closed immersion given by the reduced closure of its image (statement lines 279-285). The counted proof is short and complete: it factors through the reduced closure, uses the description of an immersion as factoring through a closed immersion into an open subscheme, and concludes by comparing two reduced closed subschemes with the same underlying set via uniqueness, which identifies the first factor as an isomorphism onto its image (proof lines 288-303). It is H2: the argument is carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the reduced induced structure and the uniqueness of reduced closed subschemes.
